$comment: DECLARED overlay — written by hand, never generated. Regenerating the schema artifact does not touch this file.

It carries what a decorator cannot express and a generator therefore must not invent. Today that is normalisation: @Transform runs an opaque lambda, so any "derived" description would really be a hand-maintained lookup wearing a generated costume.

Every entry carries its own probe, and the conformance suite runs it through plainToInstance and asserts the output. The probe IS the sentence’s operational meaning: the prose cannot drift from the behaviour, because the pair is what gets checked. A probe that fails to exercise the effect its sentence claims is visible to a reviewer, since input and expected sit beside the sentence they verify.

The opposite direction — a transform ADDED with no entry here — is caught by a canary sweep in the same suite: one rich input through every string property of all 22 DTOs, flagging any property that changes without a declared entry.

Known limit, stated rather than hidden: a future transform that is the identity on that canary would escape both checks. The rejected alternative was reading class-transformer cjs/storage internals, which has no type declarations and is an unpublished path that can move between minors.

newEmail.description: Trimmed and lowercased before validation and before the service sees it, so the stored identity matches the case-insensitive lookup and every e-mail-keyed control (brute-force counter, OTP records, reset tokens). Send any casing; the server canonicalises it.
